prompt: When does an SBOM earn its keep, according to the lesson?

choices.text: At the audit, when the regulator asks for it
choices.why: That is when it is produced as paperwork, which is the reading the lesson argues against.

choices.text: On the morning an advisory lands
choices.why: Right, when somebody asks "are we affected?": the list answers in minutes, if it was written on the build day.

choices.text: During the build, to stop vulnerable images
choices.why: Stopping images is the scanner's job; the SBOM is the record for later.

choices.text: When a customer asks for the source code
choices.why: An SBOM lists components; it is not source code.

prompt: Why must the SBOM be written on the build day rather than when the advisory arrives?

choices.text: Because syft only works inside a pipeline
choices.why: syft runs anywhere; the lesson runs it by hand first.

choices.text: Because SBOM formats change every few months
choices.why: The formats are standards; their versions are recorded in the file.

choices.text: By then the build is gone
choices.why: Right, and images that no longer run still need an answer. A list made later describes what is left, not what shipped.

choices.text: Because a scanner refuses SBOMs older than a day
choices.why: Scanning an old SBOM against new advisories is the whole point.

prompt: Which of these are among the NTIA's minimum elements of an SBOM? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the supplier
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: the dependency relationships
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: a timestamp
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: the vulnerabilities of each component
choices.why: No: an SBOM lists what is there; vulnerabilities are a question asked of it.

choices.text: the source code of each component
choices.why: No: names, versions and identifiers, not code.

prompt: How many Debian packages did syft list in linkbox's image?
Why does the lesson have syft read `localhost:5000/linkbox:main` rather than the source tree?

choices.text: The image is what ships
choices.why: Right, and only it holds the base image's packages: an SBOM describes the thing it was made from.

choices.text: syft cannot read directories
choices.why: It can, and the last section does; it finds a different set.

choices.text: Reading from the registry is faster than reading local files
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; what is described is.

choices.text: The registry signs everything it serves
choices.why: Nothing is signed until lesson 14.

prompt: An SBOM names its subject as `localhost:5000/linkbox` version `main`. What is the weakness?

choices.text: `main` is not a valid version string
choices.why: The formats accept any string as a version.

choices.text: Tomorrow, `main` names another image
choices.why: Right. The pipeline reads by a commit's tag, and lesson 14 ties the SBOM to a digest.

choices.text: The registry name contains a port
choices.why: A port in a registry name is ordinary.

choices.text: SPDX cannot describe container images
choices.why: SPDX described this one, with a DESCRIBES relationship.

prompt: Match each fact to the field where SPDX keeps it.

pairs.left: who made the document, and when

prompt: syft writes `"licenseConcluded": "NOASSERTION"` for gunicorn in SPDX. What does it mean?

choices.text: gunicorn has no licence
choices.why: It declares MIT, in licenseDeclared.

choices.text: Nobody looked beyond what the package declares
choices.why: Right: concluded is the licence somebody determined after looking, and syft did not look.

choices.text: The licence is not one allowed inside containers
choices.why: SPDX records facts; it does not judge them.

choices.text: The SPDX file is invalid
choices.why: NOASSERTION is a value the format defines.

prompt: A legal team asks for SPDX and the security platform wants CycloneDX. What does the lesson's pipeline do, and what does it cost?

choices.text: Writes one and converts it on request, at the risk of losing fields
choices.why: Conversion is possible but not what the stage does.

choices.text: Writes both from one run of syft, for a few hundred kilobytes
choices.why: Right: two -o options, one reading of the image.

choices.text: Picks CycloneDX, because security outranks licences
choices.why: The lesson says the reader decides, and keeps both.

choices.text: Runs syft twice, doubling the stage's time
choices.why: One run writes both.

prompt: In the CycloneDX file, how many components did syft record in total, files included?
Why is `packaging 26.3` in linkbox's image although `requirements.txt` never names it?

choices.text: The distroless base image ships it in its Python
choices.why: It is under /packages, installed by pip, not in the base.

choices.text: gunicorn requires it, and nothing pinned it
choices.why: Right: pip installed the newest version that day, a transitive dependency at a version nobody chose.

choices.text: syft adds it to every Python SBOM
choices.why: syft records what it finds; the image's own Python says gunicorn requires it.

choices.text: pytest pulled it in during the tests
choices.why: Test dependencies never reach the image.

prompt: In a purl such as `pkg:deb/debian/libc6@2.41-12+deb13u4?upstream=glibc`, the qualifier named ___ records the source package the binary package was built from.
Put the steps of the morning-of-the-advisory query in order.
items: an advisory names a package and its versions
list the stored SBOMs, one per image
filter each SBOM's components by name or upstream
read off which images hold an affected version

prompt: How many Debian findings did Trivy report when it scanned syft's CycloneDX SBOM of the image?
Trivy reads syft's SBOM, detects Debian 13.7 and 38 packages, and reports 0 where the image gives 162. What is the cause?

choices.text: syft missed the vulnerable packages
choices.why: The packages are all there; libc6 is in the list.

choices.text: Trivy's vulnerability database was out of date
choices.why: The same database gives 162 for the image in the same run.

choices.text: Source package names, which Trivy did not read
choices.why: Right: Debian's advisories are by source package, kept in syft's upstream qualifier. Each SBOM is correct; the pair does not work for Debian.

choices.text: Distroless images have no vulnerabilities
choices.why: The image itself scans to 162.

prompt: What does the lesson recommend before relying on a generator and a scanner together?

choices.text: Use the most popular pair
choices.why: Popularity does not show whether this pair reads this image correctly.

choices.text: Test the pair on a known image
choices.why: Right, one whose findings you already know: a zero where the image has 162 is a result you want to see in a lesson.

choices.text: Convert every SBOM to SPDX first
choices.why: From syft's SPDX, Trivy did not even find the operating system.

choices.text: Stop scanning images and scan only SBOMs
choices.why: The scan of record stays on the image itself.

prompt: Why does `sbom` come after `push` in `ci/stages`?

choices.text: syft needs the image's signature, which push adds
choices.why: Nothing is signed yet; lesson 14 adds signing.

choices.text: It describes the pushed image
choices.why: Right, read from the registry: a run that broke before push has nothing to describe.

choices.text: So that a failure in syft cannot break the build
choices.why: A failure in syft breaks the build on purpose.

choices.text: Because stages run in alphabetical order
choices.why: They run in the order the list gives.

prompt: A teammate suggests generating the SBOM from the repository with `syft dir:.` because it is faster. What would the stored list get wrong?

choices.text: Nothing, since the Python pins are the same
choices.why: The pins match, but the list adds test tools and drops every Debian package.

choices.text: It lists pytest and misses Debian
choices.why: Right: an SBOM describes what it was made from, and the image is what runs.

choices.text: It would be invalid CycloneDX
choices.why: It would be valid, and describe the wrong thing.

choices.text: It would contain the secrets in the repository
choices.why: syft lists packages; it does not copy files' contents.

prompt: An advisory lands for `packaging` below 27. linkbox's images were built over three months, and the oldest is no longer in the registry. What answers "were we exposed?" fastest?

choices.text: Pulling every image still in the registry and scanning it
choices.why: The oldest one is gone, so the answer would have a hole.

choices.text: Reading requirements.txt in each commit
choices.why: packaging was never in requirements.txt; that is the point of lesson 13.

choices.text: A loop over the SBOMs kept beside every run of the pipeline
choices.why: Right: they cover images no longer running, and they already name packaging.

choices.text: Running trivy sbom on syft's SPDX files
choices.why: From syft's SPDX, Trivy did not even find the operating system; and a jq query needs no scanner.

prompt: Which of these would syft's image SBOM not show?

choices.text: packaging 26.3, installed by pip as gunicorn's dependency
choices.why: It found it, in /packages.

choices.text: A tool copied in with COPY, with no record
choices.why: Right: no record, so at best a file with no name and no version.

choices.text: libc6 from the Debian base
choices.why: It is one of the 38 Debian packages.

choices.text: The licences of the Python packages
choices.why: It recorded them, BSD and MIT.

prompt: Lesson 14 attaches the SBOM to the image and signs it. Which two weaknesses of keeping it beside the run does that fix?

choices.text: It shrinks the file, and removes the need for jq
choices.why: Neither size nor jq is the issue.

choices.text: It adds the vulnerabilities, and the licences
choices.why: An SBOM lists components; vulnerabilities are asked of it later.

choices.text: It converts the SPDX file to CycloneDX, and deletes the logs
choices.why: Both formats are kept, and so are the logs.

choices.text: The list travels with the image, and proves the pipeline wrote it
choices.why: Right: an attestation in the registry, carrying the pipeline's signature.
